title: The inference speed of the int8 quantization version of SDXL is much slower than that of fp16
body: I am running the TensorRT 9.3 SDXL demo on an A800 GPU after manually changing the shape to 768x1344. With FP16, UNet x30 takes 2616.81 ms, the full pipeline takes 2851.01 ms, and throughput is 0.35 image/s. With INT8 using --quantization-level 3, UNet x30 takes 5550.13 ms, the pipeline takes 5785.81 ms, and throughput is 0.17 image/s.

symptoms_visible: On my A800 with the TensorRT 9.3 SDXL demo at 768x1344, INT8 level 3 runs at 0.17 image/s versus 0.35 image/s for FP16.
The UNet x30 time rises from 2616.81 ms in FP16 to 5550.13 ms in INT8, while CLIP and VAE-Dec times remain nearly unchanged.
N0.label: N0 INT8 SDXL slowdown reported

symptoms_visible: The demo does not accept quantization level 2.5 with its current command-line argument validation.
N1.label: N1 level 2.5 blocked by argument validation

symptoms_visible: After removing the integer-only choices constraint and running quantization level 2.5, UNet x30 takes 7193.33 ms, the pipeline takes 7427.78 ms, and throughput is 0.13 image/s.
N2_x.label: N2_x level 2.5 on the original stack is even slower

symptoms_visible: My latest posted A800 measurement still shows the INT8 pipeline slower than FP16, including at quantization level 2.5 on the original TensorRT 9.3 demo stack.
N3.label: N3 updated quantization stack identified as necessary

symptoms_visible: I did not post a new benchmark from my A800 after the updated GA tooling became available; my latest posted result remains 0.13 image/s at quantization level 2.5 on the earlier stack.
N_terminal.label: terminal updated workflow available but original reporter has not retested

question_patterns: Could you try the same SDXL command with quantization level 2.5 and report what happens?
Please run the demo with --quantization-level 2.5 and share either the timing table or the exact error.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Level 2.5 is not supported by the current demo argument parser. I tried level 2 instead.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Level 2.5 runs without any parser error and gives a clear speedup over FP16 on my existing setup.
The parser rejects 2.5 with an invalid-choice message before engine generation starts.

edges.comment: Issue comments c9-c11, original reporter's A800/TensorRT 9.3 system: the maintainer requested a level-2.5 probe because of the long-sequence attention limitation, but the reporter could only state that the CLI rejected that value. The reason level 2.5 was requested remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Remove the integer-only command-line choices restriction so the existing TensorRT 9.3 demo can be run with quantization level 2.5.
solution.concrete_example: Remove choices=range(1,4) from the quantization-level argument in demo/Diffusion/utilities.py, rebuild or rerun with --quantization-level 2.5, and compare the timing table.

edges.comment: Issue comments c12-c14, original reporter's system: the reporter made the requested persistent source edit and benchmarked level 2.5. The resulting 7427.78 ms pipeline time and 0.13 image/s falsified removal of the parser restriction plus level 2.5 as a sufficient fix on the original stack.

solution.intent: Treat the result as a quantization-stack and supported-kernel-path issue rather than assuming that quantizing more SDXL layers must be faster; use the updated Model Optimizer, calibration scripts, and recommended long-sequence quantization configuration.
solution.concrete_example: For SDXL sequence lengths above 512, avoid quantizing the MHA portion and use quantization level 2.5. Rebuild the engine with the updated AMMO/Model Optimizer release and its current calibration workflow rather than only editing the old demo's parser.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied only benchmark output. Maintainers explained that TensorRT did not support INT8 MHA fusion for sequence lengths above 512 and that placing Q/DQ before the fully connected layer after MHA creates an extra Quantize kernel that can reduce end-to-end performance. They subsequently identified the updated optimizer and calibration workflow as necessary.

edges.comment: Issue comments c14-c15 and c30 describe the accepted technical direction for the original report. Comments c22-c40 contain a separate affected A100 user's investigation; that deployment is not spliced into the original reporter's A800 system state.

solution.intent: Rebuild and benchmark SDXL INT8 with the current GA TensorRT and TensorRT Model Optimizer workflow, retain the long-sequence-safe quantization configuration, and ask the original reporter to verify the result on the A800 before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Move from the TensorRT 9.3 demo artifacts to the TensorRT 10.0 OSS GA and current TensorRT Model Optimizer calibration workflow, rebuild the SDXL INT8 engine, use level 2.5 for the long-sequence case, and rerun the same 768x1344 prompt and timing comparison. Another affected A100 user later reported 0.40 image/s for INT8 versus 0.36 image/s for the non-quantized model after moving to TensorRT 10, but the original A800 reporter did not post a retest.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers linked the expected improvement to the updated TensorRT/Model Optimizer environment, calibration scripts, supported kernel paths, model, and GPU. The later 12% speedup was measured by a different affected operator on an A100 and is corroborating evidence only, not verification on the original reporter's A800.

edges.comment: Issue comments c15, c21, and c30-c40: the updated GA and optimizer workflow became available. A different affected operator, ecilay, eventually measured a 12% INT8 gain on A100 with TensorRT 10; per multi-party containment this is relayed corroboration, not theNefelibata's own verification. Comments c41-c43 closed the issue for inactivity rather than because the original reporter confirmed an A800 fix.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted technical direction: the original slowdown cannot be fixed merely by quantizing more layers; SDXL sequence lengths above 512 lack the relevant INT8 MHA fusion, and the resulting Q/DQ or Quantize overhead can erase performance gains.

Must ground the diagnosis in the reported evidence: level 3 roughly doubled the A800 pipeline time, the slowdown was concentrated in UNet, and level 2.5 on the unchanged TensorRT 9.3 workflow was even slower.

Must recommend rebuilding with the current GA TensorRT, TensorRT Model Optimizer, and current calibration workflow, using the recommended long-sequence quantization configuration rather than only modifying the old parser.
Must not present removal of choices=range(1,4) and a level-2.5 run on the original stack as the complete fix; that exact attempt produced 7427.78 ms and 0.13 image/s.

Must acknowledge that achievable INT8 speedup depends on hardware, model, environment, and which layers are quantized; a speedup observed by a different A100 operator does not prove the original A800 case resolved.
Must ask the original reporter to rerun the same A800 workload with rebuilt artifacts before declaring resolution; the thread ended without that verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable ML inference user who can modify demo source, rebuild quantized engines, change framework versions, and report detailed module-level latency tables, but relies on maintainers for TensorRT kernel-support and quantization-policy guidance.
persona_hint.communication_style: Brief and results-focused; posts commands and benchmark tables, follows concrete test instructions, and asks practical questions about upcoming quantization support.
